- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then plateau or slightly decline, while true prices often show sharper corrections or mean reversion after spikes.
- Overshoots are common after sharp upward moves in history; model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits strong upward bias in the first 5–10 days of forecast, then gradually flattens — true prices often dip or stabilize earlier.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of forecast, especially when true prices show sudden drops or spikes.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion after strong upward trends; true prices often revert to lower levels faster than forecasted.
- Model overreacts to recent high prices, leading to over-optimistic forecasts in the short term.
- Model underestimates the impact of policy or market shocks in the final 5–10 days, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model tends to ignore recent downward trends in history, continuing to project upward momentum.
- Model’s forecast curve is smoother than true price movements, missing sharp reversals or volatility spikes.
